brief.headline: Nifty drops below 25650; Asian markets rally while US tech futures gain
brief.summary: Indian benchmark equities closed lower yesterday as Nifty dropped 1.07% to 25607.2 while IT stocks led losses. Meanwhile, Asian equities rallied with Nikkei 225 up 2.11% and Brent Crude eased to 91.17. Domestically, Adani Group announced capex plans of ₹2.2 trillion for FY27 alongside Sebi regulatory updates.

takeaways.text: Sebi granted Tata Steel an extension till Dec 8 for the APL Apollo Tubes open offer following shareholder concerns.
Adani Group announced a ₹2.2 trillion capex plan for FY27 while targeting the demerger of its airport business in 2027.
Sebi aims to streamline FPI onboarding time down to five business days via digital workflows.
US stock futures advanced as tech shares regained momentum, despite EU leaders failing to resolve a $1.7 trillion budget deadlock.
French third-quarter GDP contracted by 0.2%, lower than initial estimates, highlighting European economic headwinds.
Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, boosting tech stocks even as AI trade volatility persists.

sections.india: Indian markets snapped a four-week rally yesterday as Nifty declined 1.07% to 25607.2 and Sensex fell 1.17% to 83339.26. Adani Group outlined plans for a ₹2.2 trillion capital expenditure in FY27 alongside a proposed airport business demerger in 2027. Sebi extended the open offer timeline for Tata Steel regarding APL Apollo Tubes till Dec 8. Meanwhile, India's forex reserves dropped $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion.
sections.world: US equity futures rallied with S&P 500 Futures rising 0.58% and Nasdaq Futures gaining 0.64%. Asian benchmark indices opened higher, with Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng both advancing 2.11%. European Union leaders failed to break a $1.7 trillion budget deadlock, while French GDP contracted 0.2% in the third quarter. Brent Crude declined 3.64% to 91.17 while Gold climbed 3.53% to 3660.6.
sections.tech: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang returned as CEO, providing momentum to US tech stocks despite lingering volatility in AI investments. In corporate restructuring, SAP is evaluating plans to cut at least 10,000 roles as it shifts focus toward AI capabilities. In global hardware developments, Japan's JERA entered discussions with Anthropic and Meta to construct data centers near Tokyo. Additionally, Poland signed a $300 million defense agreement with Palantir Technologies.

Bloomberg's "The Opening Trade" spoke to global strategists and tech leaders about whether recent volatility signals a new era for AI investment. (Source: Bloomberg)
stories.ai_summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, driving tech shares upward. Broader market anxiety surrounding AI monetization persists.
stories.why_it_matters: Positive leadership clarity for Nvidia; broader AI spending debate stays active.

stories.title: Japan's JERA enters talks with Anthropic, Meta to build data centres
stories.summary: JERA, Japan's leading power generator, is actively engaging with prominent U.S. tech corporations to establish advanced data centers adjacent to its Tokyo-area plants. This initiative follows JERA's recent collaboration with Dell Technologies and RHAELM to boost AI infrastructure in Japan. A monumental $15 billion hyperscale data center is set for development in Chiba, attracting major players like Anthropic, Meta…
stories.ai_summary: Japan's power provider JERA is negotiating with Anthropic and Meta to build AI data centers near Tokyo.
stories.why_it_matters: Positive for global power infrastructure demand driven by AI data centers.

stories.title: Women express frustration, concern over Nvidia boss Jensen Huang's return
stories.summary: News of Jensen Huang's shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Then President Donald Trump intervened.
stories.ai_summary: The return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO triggered public debate across social platforms.
stories.why_it_matters: Social media commentary; negligible direct financial impact on equity markets.

stories.title: Poland Signs $300 Million Palantir Deal to Use AI for Defense
stories.summary: Poland will use artificial intelligence-based software from Palantir Technologies Inc. to analyze battlefield data, bucking a push by some European allies to reduce their reliance on US technology for critical defense capabilities.
stories.ai_summary: Poland executed a $300 million deal with Palantir Technologies for defense AI software to process battlefield intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: Positive for defense tech spending and Palantir's European enterprise order book.

stories.title: Chinas humanoid robot investment set to accelerate, selective commercial use expected in 2027: Morgan Stanley
stories.summary: Investment in humanoid robots is expected to accelerate in China, with improving artificial intelligence capabilities likely to support initial commercial deployments in selected tasks in 2027, even as widespread adoption remains some distance away, according to a Morgan Stanley report.

stories.title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
stories.summary: German company Q.ANT is trying to cut the amount of energy required to run AI models by using light to perform the toughest calculations.

stories.title: Fed's Dec. Meeting May Mark Turning Point for Markets: Economist
stories.summary: Mohit Kumar, chief European economist and strategist at Jefferies, discusses the outlook for the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting and its potential impact on markets. "My base case is that is the peak in hawkishness," Kumar tells Bloomberg Television. "That is, in my mind, the turning point for markets." (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Roles in AI Restructure
stories.summary: SAP SE is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era, according to people familiar with the matter, following reductions at Oracle Corp. and Microsoft Corp.

stories.title: China’s Industrial Profits Jump at Fastest Pace in Five Months
stories.summary: Earnings growth at China’s industrial enterprises hit a five-month high in October, as higher commodity costs and demand for artificial intelligence products continued to prop up prices.

stories.title: Chip Stocks Look 'Very Attractive,' State Street Says
stories.summary: Marija Veitmane of State Street says technology industry fundamentals have not weakened as much as the recent market selloff and outflows might suggest, and sees signs that sentiment is "normalizing." Speaking on Bloomberg Television, she says the pullback is an opportunity for bargain hunting, especially in semiconductors. (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.summary: Chinese stocks rebounded sharply after a rare intraday state media readout cheered investors as top policymakers pledged market liquidity support.

stories.summary: Scandal-hit Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of US chip giant Nvidia has triggered a fresh avalanche of AI-generated parody videos, highlighting how the sex-and-espionage saga has become a prime target for hyper-realistic deepfakes.
